rounds.fact: Bebo was massively popular in the UK and Ireland during the mid-2000s, at one point ranking as the third-most-visited social network in the US before AOL bought it for $850 million in 2008.
Star ratings lasted until 2010. They were retired because almost everyone rated either 5 stars or 1, so the site switched to thumbs up/down.
Encyclopedia Britannica put its entire encyclopedia online for free in 1999, a bold bet that ad revenue could replace its centuries-old subscription business, before pulling back a year later.
Rolling Stone's website launched years after the print magazine's decades-long run, and its early design mostly mirrored the print issue's contents online.
AltaVista was one of the dominant search engines before Google, and was actually first to offer a translation tool (Babel Fish) that became hugely popular in its own right.
